summary: The Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) gives interest-free loans to Nigerian students in public (federal and state) universities, polytechnics, colleges of education and approved vocational schools. It pays your school fees directly to your institution and can also pay you an upkeep allowance (₦20,000 a month in current guides). You repay only after you finish school and NYSC — repayment starts two years after NYSC — so the 'winners' are simply eligible students who apply correctly and on time.
lookfor: You are Nigerian and enrolled in a public tertiary institution that has uploaded its student list to NELFUND
Your NIN, JAMB registration number and school records all match (same names, same date of birth)
Your BVN and bank account are in your own name so upkeep can be paid
Your admission letter is uploaded clearly
You apply inside the session's window — no essays, no interview, no grade cut-off
cycle: Reported for 2026/2027: the portal opened around 23 September 2026 with a deadline reported as 31 December 2026 (confirm on nelf.gov.ng and @nelfund; last session's deadline was extended twice into March 2026). Funds are usually paid within weeks of approval once your school confirms you.

eligibility.q: Are you a Nigerian citizen with a National Identification Number (NIN)?
eligibility.no: Enrol for your NIN at a NIMC centre first. Non-Nigerians cannot use NELFUND.

eligibility.q: Are you admitted to (or studying in) a public university, polytechnic, college of education or approved vocational institution in Nigeria?
eligibility.no: Students in private institutions are not covered. Look at your state bursary board, company scholarships or private-school bursaries.

eligibility.q: Has your institution uploaded its verified student list to NELFUND for this session?
eligibility.no: Ask your school's Student Affairs or Bursary office (many have a NELFUND desk) to upload or update the list. You cannot complete the application until your school is on the portal.

eligibility.q: Do you have a bank account and BVN in your own name?
eligibility.no: Open a personal account with your NIN and get a BVN at any bank before applying.

eligibility.q: Do you have your JAMB registration number (or matriculation details) and admission letter?
eligibility.no: Recover your JAMB number from your JAMB profile or result slip, and print your admission letter from your school or JAMB CAPS.
NELFUND's application flow is built around undergraduate, ND/HND and NCE students with JAMB records. Postgraduates should check the current FAQ on nelf.gov.ng and also consider other awards.

steps.title: Understand the loan before you borrow
steps.why: It is a loan, not a gift. Knowing the terms helps you decide how much to request.
do: Note what it covers: institutional (school) fees paid to your school, and an optional monthly upkeep allowance paid to you.
Note the terms: 0% interest; repayment starts two years after NYSC, by deduction from salary (or profit if self-employed).
Decide: fees only, upkeep only, or both.
Tell your parent or guardian you are applying.
tips: If your family can pay fees, you might request upkeep only — you will owe less later.
avoid: Thinking NELFUND is a grant that never needs repaying.
check: I know what I am borrowing and when repayment starts

steps.title: Learn the one official address and avoid scams
steps.why: Fake NELFUND sites have stolen students' NIN and bank details. NELFUND says the only official portal is on nelf.gov.ng.
do: Bookmark https://www.nelf.gov.ng/ and use only the 'Apply' link on it.
Check the address bar every time: it must end in nelf.gov.ng.
Follow only verified handles (@nelfund on X and Instagram) for news.
Report suspicious links to info@nelf.gov.ng.
tips: The application is free. Anyone who asks you to pay to apply or to 'speed up' your loan is a scammer.
avoid: Clicking WhatsApp links like 'nelfund-student-loan-2025.po-rt-al.com' — NELFUND named this as fake.
check: I have bookmarked the real site

links.t: Channels TV: NELFUND warns against fake websites

steps.title: Confirm your school is on NELFUND
steps.why: The portal verifies you against the student list your school uploads. If the school has not uploaded, you will be stuck.
do: Visit your Dean of Student Affairs or the school's NELFUND desk/office.
Ask: Has the school uploaded this session's list? Is my name and matric/JAMB number on it?
Ask for your school's NELFUND deadline (some schools set earlier internal dates).
If you are a fresher, ask when new students will be added.
tips: Join your faculty or SUG channel where the NELFUND desk posts updates.
avoid: Assuming you were uploaded because a friend was.
check: My school confirmed I am on the list

steps.title: Fix your NIN, JAMB and bank details so they match
steps.why: Most failed applications and unpaid upkeep come from mismatched names, dates of birth or unvalidated bank details.
do: Print your NIN slip and compare your full name and date of birth with your JAMB record and school record.
If anything differs, correct it first (NIMC for NIN; JAMB for JAMB data; your school's records office).
Make sure you can access the email and phone number linked to your NIN.
Confirm your BVN is linked to an account in your own name.
tips: Use the same spelling of your name everywhere — even a missing middle name can cause a mismatch.
avoid: Using a parent's or friend's bank account — upkeep payments to such accounts fail.
check: NIN, JAMB, school and bank details all match

links.t: Nairametrics: upkeep payments failed for thousands due to bank details (Oct 2026)

steps.title: Scan your admission letter and student ID
steps.why: The admission letter is the key upload; a school ID card helps.
do: Get your admission letter (from your school portal or JAMB CAPS).
Scan it clearly as PDF or JPEG.
Scan your school ID card if you have one.
Keep file sizes small (under the limit the portal shows).
tips: Use a scanner app that crops edges and boosts contrast.
avoid: Uploading a dark or cut-off photo.
check: My admission letter scan is clear and readable

steps.title: Create your account on the NELFUND portal
steps.why: Verification happens at sign-up. If it works, your name and photo appear.
do: Go to https://www.nelf.gov.ng/ and click Apply (it opens portal.nelf.gov.ng).
Choose 'Get started', select Nigerian and choose your institution.
Enter your JAMB registration number and date of birth; check that your name and photo appear.
Enter your NIN; check that your name appears.
Create a password and verify your email.
tips: Use a laptop or phone with good data; do it at quiet times (early morning).
avoid: Creating several accounts — it can flag duplicates.
check: I can log in and see my verified details

steps.title: Complete your profile and bank details
steps.why: Upkeep is paid to the account you enter here.
do: Fill phone, home address and state.
Check the auto-filled school details: course, department, level, session.
Enter your BVN, bank name and account number.
Save and re-check every digit.
tips: Screenshot the confirmation of your bank details for your records.
avoid: Typing the wrong account number — failed payments take a long time to fix.
check: My profile and bank details are correct

steps.title: Request the loan and submit
steps.why: This is the actual application. Submit well before the deadline.
do: On the dashboard, click Loan (or Apply for loan).
Choose institutional fees, upkeep, or both.
Upload your admission letter (required) and school ID (optional).
Read the terms and conditions, then review the total amount.
Submit and screenshot the confirmation screen.
tips: Read the terms fully: false information is a crime under the Act.
avoid: Leaving it until the final week, when the portal slows down.
check: I have a screenshot showing my application was submitted

steps.title: Track your status and fix problems
steps.why: Your school must confirm you before money moves. Catching a problem early prevents months of delay.
do: Log in weekly and check your application status.
If it is stuck, visit your school's NELFUND desk and ask them to confirm your record.
For portal issues, use NELFUND's support chat at nelfund.esupport.ng.
Keep all emails from @nelf.gov.ng addresses.
tips: Write down any ticket numbers support gives you.
avoid: Giving your password or OTP to anyone 'helping' you.

steps.title: Receive funds and re-apply each session
steps.why: Fees go to your school and upkeep to your account. You need to apply again each new session.
do: Check with the school bursary that your fees were received; collect your receipt.
Check your bank account for monthly upkeep.
Keep records of every payment — they are your loan balance.
Set a reminder for next session's window (usually announced around September–October).
tips: NELFUND plans to move fee payments to a digital token system — watch official updates.
avoid: Paying fees twice: confirm with the bursary before paying yourself.
check: I have a reminder for next session

links.t: Premium Times: NELFUND extends deadline (2025/26 session)

steps.title: Plan for repayment after NYSC
steps.why: Repayment starts two years after NYSC. Planning now avoids surprises.
do: Note your total borrowed each year.
Expect deductions from your salary through your employer once repayment starts (the original Act set 10% of salary; check current rules).
Keep your contact details on the portal up to date after graduation.
If you cannot find work, check NELFUND's current guidance on deferral.
tips: Keep your NELFUND login details safe after graduation.
avoid: Ignoring NELFUND messages after you leave school.
check: I know when and how I will repay

faq.q: Does it cost money to apply?
faq.a: No. The application is free on nelf.gov.ng.

faq.q: Do I need a guarantor or proof of low family income?
faq.a: No. The 2024 Act removed the guarantor rule and the ₦500,000 family-income cap.
No. NELFUND covers public tertiary institutions (and approved vocational schools).
Current guides say ₦20,000 a month. Check the amount shown on the portal when you apply.

faq.q: My name or photo didn't appear when I entered my JAMB number. What now?
faq.a: Your records may not match or your school may not have uploaded you. Check with your school's NELFUND desk, then contact NELFUND support.
